newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev closes softer on c.bank dollar buying.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev closes softer on c.bank dollar buying.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed softer at 1,497-1,502 per dollar after a 1,493-1,499 opening as dollar buying by the central bank stirred a dollar-bearish market, dealers said.
"The lev edged down due to central bank dollar bidding at 1,497-1,499 levs. If the central bank had not purchased foreign currency the lev could have firmed in very thin volumes," one dealer said.
Central bank officials were not available for comment.

Traders said dollar demand from commercial bank and clients was low throughout the day, while domestic and foreign investors offered large foreign currency volumes for levs, eyeing high yielding local debt paper.
Foreign investors bought Bulgarian government securities worth 81 billion levs and $128 million in March and April, central bank figures showed.

Yields to maturity on lev-denominated six-, nine- and 12-month, floating interest T-bill issues auctioned on Monday were 41.02, 64.27 and 84.78 percent, respectively, under the current main interest rate of 6.20 percent monthly.
Interest on the paper is pegged to the main interest rate and adjusted each time the rate is changed by the central bank. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
